# Data provenance (generated by DataReportTest, world created 21 Nov 2026; facts refreshed 22 Nov 2026)

What each game's starting world is built from. "Estimated" means the source did not give the
fact and the game filled it in. "Position from recent matches" is worked out from real match data
(Valorant: agents played over 90 days; Dota 2: lanes and farm in pro matches since 2024), not
listed by a source (shown as *Estimated* on the player page's **Data provenance**
card). Ratings and attributes are always game estimates, never real measurements.

## Sources and limits

| Game | Source of current rosters | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| League of Legends | lolesports.com league pages (snapshot 20 Nov 2026; LJL, PCS and VCS added 22 Nov 2026 as tier-2 leagues under the LCP, `scripts/data/rosters_lol_tier2.py`); birthdays / nationalities from Leaguepedia (lol.fandom.com) | Verified rosters; facts matched only when the real name matches (same-handle mix-ups such as Peyz, Ruler, Caps, Knight are rejected) |
| Valorant | vlr.gg team pages (snapshot); birthdays / real names from the VALORANT Esports Wiki (whole Players table + handle redirects, Cargo API) | Verified rosters and nationalities (vlr.gg flags); current players' positions from agents played; former players' positions are game assignments (vlr.gg's stats pages could not be fetched) |
| Counter-Strike 2 | Valve Regional Standings on github.com (snapshot); nationalities / birthdays from bo3.gg | Verified rosters; shared nicknames are settled by team or by the only ranked player (ambiguous ones are left estimated); no open source lists CS2 positions, so every position is a game assignment |
| Dota 2 | OpenDota (opendota.com, snapshot) | Verified team names and handles; positions from lanes and farm in pro matches (OpenDota SQL explorer, 2024-26); nationality by agreement of Wikidata, Valve's pro-player country and the Steam flag (none is reliable alone: Valve's unset value reads "Afghanistan", Steam flags are often jokes); birthdays only where Wikidata has them |
| Mobile Legends | MPL ID and MPL PH official sites (id-mpl.com, ph-mpl.com; snapshot) | Verified rosters for two leagues; fictional leagues fill the other regions. No open source has MLBB birthdays (Liquipedia rate-limits this project, the MLBB esports Fandom wiki has 11 pages), so ages and former players' nationalities are estimates |
| Wild Rift | Wild Rift Esports Wiki — **early 2021** | Historical rosters, labelled on every team page; no current source could be used |
| Honor of Kings | none usable | Liquipedia answered HTTP 429 (rate limited) and earlier a CAPTCHA, which this project does not bypass; Wikipedia has no rosters. HoK leagues, teams and players are fictional and labelled so. With a Liquipedia (LPDB) API key the HoK and Wild Rift packs could be refreshed |

Characters: 724 champions / heroes / agents from game data sources (Riot Data Dragon, wildrift.leagueoflegends.com, pvp.qq.com, mlbbhub.com, OpenDota, valorant-api.com; 20 Nov 2026). CS2 has weapons, not characters.

## Database audit, second pass (22 Nov 2026)

`scripts/data/player_facts_more.py` (after `player_facts_fix.py`):

- **Same handle, different person.** Matches made on the handle alone (no real name to compare) were
  the main source of wrong nationalities. A fact is now refused when it contradicts the nationality
  the roster source lists (e.g. Chinese-league Valorant players "Master", "Life", "nothing", "PHO"
  had been given Brazilian, Korean, Dutch and American facts; a Brazilian "Sato" a Swedish one), and
  a Wikidata match pointing to another continent than the club's country is refused.
- **Valorant:** the whole VALORANT Esports Wiki player table and its redirects: 127 more players with
  real birthdays and names (birthday estimates 90% → 75%).
- **League of Legends:** players still without facts looked up through Leaguepedia's handle redirects
  (33 more).
- **Dota 2:** positions for 275 players from their lanes and farm in pro matches (game assignments
  78% → 4%); nationalities re-decided by agreement of three sources; Valve's unset "af"/"ax"
  values (read as Afghanistan / Åland) removed.
- **CS2:** 7 same-nickname mix-ups re-picked by team, 3 ambiguous ones removed.
- **Wild Rift:** wiki-listed positions are no longer counted as estimates; the wiki has almost no
  player records (birthdays) for the 2021 rosters.
- Liquipedia answered HTTP 429; per its terms nothing was retried there.

## Mobile Legends fixes (22 Nov 2026, third pass)

- **Wrong people matched by handle.** Six MLBB players had been given the facts of an unrelated
  Wikidata person with the same handle, and the continent check let three through (RRQ's ARTHUR
  shown as a Korean "Park Mir" born 2000; others with Chinese, Taiwanese, Swedish, South African and
  Italian facts). All six were removed; handle-only Wikidata matches are no longer used for MLBB or
  Honor of Kings (their rosters list no real names), both in `player_facts_fix.py` and in the game.
- **Kairi (ONIC):** Filipino, born 21 Sep 2005, full name from Liquipedia (CC BY-SA 3.0, one API
  request); the second request was rate-limited (HTTP 429), so nothing more was fetched there.
- **Team Liquid PH's Teddy** had no position: the official site writes "Goldlane" without a space;
  the parser and the snapshot now read it as Gold lane.
- Still estimated (shown as such on player pages): other current MLBB players' nationalities (taken
  from the league's country, so Filipino imports in MPL ID can show as Indonesian) and all MLBB
  birth dates — no open source the project may use lists them.

## Competition rules (five expansions, 22 Nov 2026)

Each competition edition records the ruleset it was planned with (`Competition.rules`), shown on its
Entrants tab and on the Road screen with what is official and what is the game's:

- **League of Legends 2026** — official in part, from the LoL Esports 2026 handbook
  (https://lolesports.com/en-SG/season/115547545029543948/handbook): First Stand takes each region's
  Split 1 winner plus the LCK and LPL runners-up; MSI takes CBLOL's top team and the top two of every
  other region; the MSI winner qualifies directly for Worlds and the runner-up's region gets an extra
  seed. Worlds slots per region and split formats are the game's. Later seasons: the same rules,
  labelled as a fictional continuation.
- **VALORANT 2027** — official announcement (Riot, 8 Apr 2026,
  https://valorantesports.com/en-US/news/the-new-valorant-champions-tour): open qualifiers feed two
  Cups per territory that replace league play; Kickoff, Masters Seoul, Masters Valencia, Champions
  Austin; Champions = top two per territory on points plus Cup 2's top two; partner teams seeded into
  later qualifier rounds with no automatic international place. Masters slot counts are the game's.
  2026 keeps a fictional split-league preset; 2029 onwards is a labelled fictional continuation.
- **Counter-Strike 2** — method from Valve's published Regional Standings
  (https://github.com/ValveSoftware/counter-strike_regional_standings): standings invite teams to the
  later stages, everyone else plays open qualifiers. The standings formula is the game's approximation.
- **Dota 2, MLBB, Honor of Kings, Wild Rift** — fictional presets modelled on public structures;
  no official rulebook was used.
- **Development circuits** (amateur, university, Game Changers clubs and events) are fictional.

No Liquipedia or Fandom pages were requested for this phase; no roster or player data was changed.

## Real history before the save (honours.json, 24 Nov 2026)

`src/data/real/honours.json`, read by `mgmt/HistoryBook`:

| Part | Source | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| League of Legends | Leaguepedia Cargo API (lol.fandom.com), tables `Tournaments`, `TournamentResults`, `TournamentPlayers`; a few polite requests, nothing bypassed | 440 events 2011–2026: every World Championship (2017 onwards from the parent event page), MSI, First Stand, EWC, Mid-Season Cup, IEM, KeSPA / Demacia Cups and the top domestic leagues (LCK / OGN Champions, LPL, LEC / EU LCS, LCS / NA LCS, LMS, PCS, VCS, LJL, CBLOL, LCP, LTA, TCL, LLA, OPL, LCL, GPL). Champions and runners-up with their players (coaches left out). A split's regular season is not counted as a title when the split has playoffs. |
| CS (CS:GO / CS2) | Compiled for this game from public records | Every Major from DreamHack Winter 2013 to the BLAST.tv Austin Major 2025 (winner, runner-up, rosters where reliably known); HLTV player of the year 2013–2024. |
| Dota 2 | Compiled | The International 2011–2025 (winner, runner-up, rosters where reliably known). |
| VALORANT | Compiled | Masters and Champions 2021–2025. |
| Not included | — | Honor of Kings (the game's HoK players are fictional), Wild Rift, MLBB, domestic leagues of CS / Dota / VALORANT. The VALORANT and Wild Rift fan wikis hold almost no tournament data; Liquipedia was not used (it refused automated access earlier); Wikipedia's API was rate-limiting this network. |

Compiled entries were not checked against a live source in this export and may contain gaps; they are labelled
`"src":"compiled"` in the file. Players are matched by game and handle (case and punctuation ignored), and only
in real-data worlds: a fictional world has no real history. Scoring: world titles 12 points, international titles
5–9, league titles 2–4, cups 1.5, a lost final 30% of the title; compiled events count double because only the
biggest events of those games are recorded.

| Game | Events added | Source | With the champions' players |

* **League History tabs.** VCT and MPL leagues' History tabs show their region's events: VCT Americas
  lists its Kickoffs and Stages, and before them the Challengers of North America, Brazil and Latin
  America.
* **Not covered:**
  * the other MPL Indonesia seasons, which the site no longer keeps (old season addresses show the
    current season);
  * MPL Philippines, whose site loads results with JavaScript;
  * M-series and MSC;
  * CS events before bo3.gg's records (2020), other than the Majors;
  * Dota 2 events without a premium tier on OpenDota;
  * Wild Rift and HoK.
* **Missing line-ups.** Some finals have no line-up, where the source lists none (OpenDota has no player
  records for many older Dota 2 finals).

## Real staff (staff.json, 25 Nov 2026)

`src/data/real/staff.json`, built by `scripts/data/staff.py` and read by `mgmt/Staffing.loadReal`: 616 people.

| Part | Source | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| League of Legends | Leaguepedia Cargo API (lol.fandom.com): `TournamentPlayers` joined with `Tournaments` (coach, head coach, assistant and positional coach entries of 2025–2026 events and of every champion and runner-up in honours.json), `TeamRedirects` (team names), `Players` (name, nationality, birth date, retired). Read-only queries, three seconds apart, responses cached. | 164 staff at 78 of the 80 LoL teams of the snapshot (each team's most recent tournament roster; "Head Coach" where marked, otherwise the first coach listed leads), 309 former coaches, 1,293 coaching credits at finals since 2011. |
| MLBB | Official MPL Indonesia / Philippines team pages (already in rosters.json) | 37 coaches, assistant coaches and analysts. |
| VALORANT | vlr.gg team pages (already in rosters.json) | 87 head coaches, coaches, assistants, performance coaches, analysts and managers. |
| Wild Rift | Wild Rift Esports Wiki pages (wildrift.json, early 2021) | 2 head coaches. |
| CS2, Dota 2, VALORANT titles | Compiled from public records (`scripts/data/compiled_staff.json`) | Head coaches whose role and titles are well documented: XTQZZZ, B1ad3, hally, sycrone, maaRaa, zonic, RobbaN, valens, dastan (CS); Silent, Blitz, Aui_2000 (Dota 2); bonkar, alecks, Potter, bzkA, kaplan, mini, Chet (VALORANT) with their Major / TI / Champions / Masters titles. |
| Not included | — | Honor of Kings (fictional players and staff); CS2 and Dota 2 coaches beyond the compiled list (Liquipedia, HLTV and the fan wikis were not used: refused automated access or protected). Those clubs get generated staff. |

Coaches are matched to teams by game and team name; a coach whose club is not in the game (or who has no club)
starts as a free agent in the staff market, as do retired coaches. Their ability is not real data: it is estimated
from their club's level and their titles (head coach titles in full, other coaching credits 40%; compiled titles
count double, as for players). One note on the fetch: a re-run of the script lost its cache (a hashing bug, since
fixed) and Leaguepedia answered "rate limited"; the script stopped there and the earlier complete result was
reused — nothing was retried or worked around.

## Finals MVPs and career moves (careers.json, 25 Nov 2026)

* **Finals MVPs** (`scripts/data/finals_mvp.py`, honours.json field `fm`): Leaguepedia Cargo API —
  `Tournaments` (event pages) and `MatchSchedule` (the last series between each LoL champion and
  runner-up, and its MVP where the page records one): 129 of 436 LoL finals. Other games have no
  finals MVP in the data (the competition History tab says so).
* **Stage rosters fixed** (`scripts/data/honours_rosters_fix.py`): a few stage records (groups, a regular
  season) had merged several teams' players into one champion or runner-up roster (e.g. Bin and Knight
  listed with three LPL teams in one year). Rosters of more than nine names were emptied (21 rosters);
  the team names stay.
* **Career moves** (`scripts/data/careers.py` → `src/data/real/careers.json`, read by `mgmt/Careers`):
  4,332 people.

| Part | Source | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| League of Legends | Leaguepedia Cargo API: `Tenures` joined to `RosterChanges` (team, join and leave month, role: position or staff role). A wiki career is used only when it shares a team with what the snapshot knows about the person (83 left out as probably another person with the same handle). | 997 players and coaches with exact spells. |
| VALORANT | VALORANT Esports Wiki Cargo API, same tables | 12 people: the wiki answered "rate limited" after the first chunks; the script stopped there (no retry) and the result was built from what had been fetched. |
| Every game | The snapshot itself: current roster (rosters.json, wildrift.json), last team seen (history.json), champion and runner-up rosters (honours.json), coaches' titles (staff.json) | Teams by year, not exact dates; not a complete record. The page says which kind it shows. |

Disambiguated Leaguepedia pages (for example a handle shared by several players, kept as "Knight (Zhuo Ding)")
were not matched in this pass; those players show the snapshot's teams by year. Liquipedia (MLBB, HoK, Dota 2,
CS2) was not used: it refused automated access earlier (HTTP 429) and is not retried.

## Past rosters by team (pastRosters.json, 25 Nov 2026)

`scripts/data/past_rosters.py` → `src/data/real/pastRosters.json` (read by `mgmt/PastRosters`, team page →
Past rosters → "Before the save"). Who played for each real team, year by year, with the staff where a source
lists them. 529 teams; 1,098 requests, every response cached; nothing was rate-limited.

| Game | Source | Teams | Years | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| League of Legends | Games of Legends (gol.gg) season team pages (robots.txt allows them; 1.5 s apart): the players who played for the team that season, their position and flag. Joined with the Leaguepedia tenures of careers.json (months, staff). | 168 of 177 | 2011–2026 | 2013 has few gol.gg teams; earlier years come from Leaguepedia tenures and title rosters only. |
| Dota 2 | OpenDota public SQL explorer: every premium/professional league match since 2012, per team and player (first and last match). Players with at least 5 games; names from OpenDota's pro-player list. | 65 of 69 | 2011–2026 | A club that changed its OpenDota team id keeps only the current id's matches. Positions come from the game's player when the person is in the game. |
| VALORANT | vlr.gg team transaction logs (joins, departures, staff; 1 s apart). | 70 of 72 | 2020–2026 | Dates to the day; positions from the game's player. |
| CS2 | Valve Regional Standings (monthly global and regional standings with five-player rosters, Aug 2024 on) and the Major champion / runner-up rosters (honours.json). | 162 of 162 | 2013–2026 | Before Aug 2024 only the Major finalists' rosters: most CS2 teams have only recent years. |
| MLBB | MPL Indonesia (Season 4 on) and MPL Philippines (Season 6 on) official team pages; an old team page redirects to the club's current one, which links a club's seasons. | 26 of 28 | 2019–2026 | Season → year: S1–S2 2018, S3–S4 2019 … S17–S18 2026. Early seasons list classes (fighter, tank) rather than lanes. |
| Wild Rift | Wild Rift Esports Wiki rosters (2021, wildrift.json) | 38 of 38 | 2021 | The only year with a source. |
| Honor of Kings | none | — | — | The HoK teams are fictional. |

How the years are built: a spell counts in every year it covers, except that a spell starting in November or
December counts from the next year, and one ending in January stops the year before, so pre-season signings
don't show up in the old year. A person listed as staff and as a player in the same year (title rosters list
coaches) is shown as staff. Earlier names of a club are joined in from a short list of renames (e.g. SK Telecom
T1 → T1, Samsung Galaxy / KSV → Gen.G, DAMWON → Dplus KIA, MAD Lions → Movistar KOI, Excel → GIANTX, Suning →
Weibo Gaming); slot purchases are not joined. Roles that are neither playing nor coaching (streamer, content
creator) are left out.

**Historical teams.** Champions and finalists of the real events (honours.json) that are not teams of the
snapshot join as well: 150 dormant real teams (132 LoL, 9 Dota 2, 6 CS2, 3 VALORANT), such as Taipei
Assassins, Azubu Frost or Moscow Five, with their rosters by year from the same sources (career records,
title rosters, Games of Legends). They are matched by exact name only, after the game's own teams, so no
roster of a current team changes.

**Every player on these rosters, and every player of the career and honours records, is in the game.**
The 3,175 who were not in the real-data snapshot or the history pack join a new world as real free agents
(6,037 different past-roster players across the six games, plus the career-record players on no roster).
A former player who coaches today also has their staff page. What the game knows about them, and what it
estimates:

| Fact | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| Handle, teams by year | the past rosters (sources above) |
| Position | the most frequent position on those rosters (LoL, MLBB, Wild Rift), else the facts snapshot, else a game assignment (shown as estimated on the player page; VALORANT and CS2 rosters list no positions) |
| Nationality | the roster flag (VALORANT, LoL), else the facts snapshot, else estimated from the last club's country |
| Birth date | the facts snapshot when it has the player, else estimated from the debut year (about 19 at the debut) |
| Real name | the facts snapshot only |
| Ratings | game estimates: a little below today's real average, lower for every season since the last one on a roster |

They are added after the rest of the world, from their own random streams, and after the youth intake's
target size is set, so every other team, player and coach comes out exactly as without them, and the
oldest retire over the next seasons (unsigned players aged 33+) without a matching wave of new prospects.

**Photos of past players (26 Nov 2026, `scripts/data/past_pictures.py`).** 758 photo links were added
for players without one:

| Source | Photos | How a match is made |
|---|---|---|
| vlr.gg player pages (VALORANT) | 330 | player id from the cached transaction pages |
| bo3.gg player list (CS2) | 230 | nickname |
| LoL Esports gateway (LoL) | 152 | handle plus a team the player was on; archived teams list their last rosters |
| Wikidata / Wikimedia Commons, free licences (any game) | 46 | handle plus the real name, a team, or the country |

These are links only, nothing is copied. Players still without a photo keep the generated portrait: LoL
2,100, MLBB 507, Dota 2 382, VALORANT 263, Wild Rift 210 and CS2 73. Most LoL past-player photos are on
Leaguepedia, which was not queried again after it rate-limited this snapshot's requests. Liquipedia (Dota 2,
MLBB) answered 429. Wikidata answered 429 to a second, wider query, which was not retried.

## Special additions (special.json, 25 Nov 2026)

Added at the player's request, not from a data source, and labelled on the team page:

* **Los Ratones in the LEC** as an eleventh team, with the line-up of their 2025–26 run (Baus, Velja, Nemesis,
  Crownie, Rekkles; real names, nationalities and birthdays from the facts snapshot), Caedrel (the club's
  founder) as head coach and Shaves (their real 2025–26 assistant coach) as assistant coach. Starting team
  strength 72, like SK Gaming or Team Heretics. In reality the club has no LEC place, and YamatoCannon, their
  head coach in 2025–26, stays at Cloud9 Kia in the game.
